skills.name: claude-parallel-tdd-planner
skills.description: Create architecture-based parallel TDD plans and execution handoffs for any coding agent, with goal options, progress/ETA supervision, Whitebox acceptance, and OpenSpec consistency/archive/readback closeout. Use for agent parallel planning, Claude TDD plans, or implementation handoffs; planning alone does not start product execution.

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

interface.shortDescription: Review a diff on standards and spec

skills.name: comet
skills.description: Comet workflow entry. Use when the user invokes /comet or asks to use Comet without choosing Native or Classic; load Native or Classic from project configuration.

interface.shortDescription: Load Native or Classic from project configuration

skills.name: comet-any
skills.description: Create or upgrade a Comet Classic workflow Skill via Comet Creator. Not for general Skill authoring, cleanup, or review.

interface.shortDescription: Create or upgrade a Comet Classic workflow Skill

skills.name: comet-archive
skills.description: Archive and deliver a Classic change. Use when the user invokes /comet-archive or Classic Runtime enters Archive or resumes delivery.

interface.shortDescription: Archive and complete the user-selected delivery

skills.name: comet-build
skills.description: Plan, implement, and accept Classic tasks. Use when the user invokes /comet-build or Classic Runtime enters Build or returns to Build for repairs.

interface.displayName: Comet Classic Phase 3: Plan and Build
interface.shortDescription: Plan or resume implementation and verify completed tasks

skills.name: comet-classic
skills.description: Comet Classic workflow entry. Use when the user explicitly invokes /comet-classic, asks to start or resume Classic, or resume-probe returns auto_resume for one unambiguously recoverable active Classic change.

interface.shortDescription: Comet Classic workflow: OpenSpec + Matt methods

skills.name: comet-design
skills.description: Complete the Classic technical design and obtain user confirmation. Use when the user invokes /comet-design or Classic Runtime enters Design.

interface.shortDescription: Discuss technical choices and confirm the design with the user

skills.name: comet-hotfix
skills.description: Use the Classic preset to repair a localized defect. Use when the user explicitly invokes /comet-hotfix, selects hotfix, or resumes workflow: hotfix.

interface.shortDescription: Reproduce, fix, and verify a localized defect

skills.name: comet-memory
skills.description: Use when Comet must decide whether a bounded semantic review packet contains a personal memory worth creating, updating, forgetting, or skipping.

interface.shortDescription: Review comet.memory.review.v1 and return fixed actions

skills.name: comet-open
skills.description: Create a Classic change, clarify its requirements, and obtain user confirmation. Use when the user invokes /comet-open or Classic enters Open or resumes initialization.

interface.shortDescription: Create a change and confirm its requirements with the user

skills.name: comet-review
skills.description: Manually review the implementation diff for the current Comet change. Report correctness, security, and edge-case issues without advancing the workflow.

interface.shortDescription: Review the current change without writing or advancing workflow

skills.name: comet-tweak
skills.description: Use the Classic preset for a lightweight adjustment within one change. Use when the user explicitly invokes /comet-tweak, selects tweak, or resumes workflow: tweak.

interface.shortDescription: Complete a light or moderate change with matching specs

skills.name: comet-verify
skills.description: Verify a Classic change and record the results. Use when the user invokes /comet-verify or Classic Runtime enters Verify.

interface.shortDescription: Verify the change and return failed checks to Build

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

interface.shortDescription: Diagnose hard bugs and regressions

skills.name: grill-me
skills.description: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding, resolving each branch of the decision tree. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on their design, or mentions "grill me".

skills.name: grilling
skills.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan or design. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan before building, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

skills.name: multi-agent-consensus-review
skills.description: Run a read-only architecture, code, or general review across Claude Code, zcode, and Codex Agent with independent scoring, a hard unanimous-consensus gate, and evidence-based debate when any participant disagrees. Use when a review must not pass by majority vote, average score, or initiator override, and must end with a defensible conclusion plus an executable next-step plan.

interface.shortDescription: Unanimous architecture and code review gate
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $multi-agent-consensus-review to run a unanimous architecture or code review across Claude Code, zcode, and Codex.

skills.name: openspec-lifecycle-guard
skills.description: Use when creating, editing, validating, or archiving OpenSpec changes in any repository, or when spec/task debt is suspected — enforces evidence-based task completion, strict validation, and archive readiness.

skills.name: ponytail
skills.description: Lazy senior dev mode: the smallest change that fully solves the task, and a reply a busy human understands in one read. Use on any coding task (writing, fixing, refactoring, reviewing, choosing dependencies) and when the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "simplest solution", "yagni", or complains about over-engineering or bloat. Levels: lite, full (default), ultra.

skills.name: ponytail
skills.description: Lazy senior dev mode: the smallest change that fully solves the task, and a reply a busy human understands in one read. Use on any coding task (writing, fixing, refactoring, reviewing, choosing dependencies) and when the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "simplest solution", "yagni", or complains about over-engineering or bloat. Levels: lite, full (default), ultra.

skills.name: ponytail-audit
skills.description: Quality audit of a whole repo: bugs, security holes, what breaks under real load, risky code without tests, slow paths, and what to delete, merge or split. Ranked, each finding explained in plain English. One-shot report, changes nothing. Use for "audit this codebase", "review the whole repo", "find bloat", "what can I delete", /ponytail-audit.

skills.name: ponytail-debt
skills.description: List every `shortcut:` comment (and older `ponytail:` ones) as a debt ledger. One-shot report, changes nothing. Use for "ponytail debt", "what did ponytail defer", "list the shortcuts", /ponytail-debt.

skills.name: ponytail-gain
skills.description: Show ponytail's measured savings (code, cost, speed) from the benchmark. One-shot display. Use for /ponytail-gain, "what does ponytail save", "ponytail impact".

skills.name: ponytail-help
skills.description: Quick reference for ponytail levels, skills and commands. One-shot display. Use for /ponytail-help, "ponytail help", "how do I use ponytail".

skills.name: ponytail-review
skills.description: Quality review of a change: is the logic right, is it safe, does it hold under real load, is risky code tested, is it fast enough, and is every line needed. Reads the connected code, not only the diff. Each finding is explained in plain English. Use for "review this", "code review", "review the last commit", "review my PR", "is this over-engineered", /ponytail-review.

skills.name: tdd
skills.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

interface.shortDescription: Test-driven red-green-refactor

skills.name: test-authoring
skills.description: 从需求、规范、代码变更和缺陷记录设计测试用例，并按授权编写或补充可执行测试代码、数据夹具与测试自检。 当用户要求“写测试用例”“根据需求设计边界/异常/权限场景”“补单测/集成/契约/属性/E2E 测试”“生成可交付测试包”时使用。 支持只设计用例和设计加自动化两种模式，复用项目现有框架，产出可追溯交接包。 仅验收、浏览器取证、判断功能是否通过转 whitebox-verify；不承担业务验收结论，不因编写测试而修改产品实现。

interface.shortDescription: Design traceable cases and author meaningful executable tests
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $test-authoring to design or write traceable tests and hand them to independent acceptance.

skills.name: whitebox-verify
skills.description: 验证代码变更和真实用户流程，排查功能不工作，执行 E2E/end-to-end、白盒验证、Journey 验收、浏览器交互检查和截图取证。 当用户要求“前端改好了帮我验收”“检查按钮/表单/登录/保存是否生效”“在内置浏览器验证并截图”“验证修复/回归/跨服务终态”时使用。 对含 UI 的功能验收优先发现并使用当前 agent harness 原生浏览器，连接请求证据、截图与业务终态回读；本地无 UI 规则走 Slice。 写测试、设计用例、生成自动化脚本转 test-authoring；本技能只做独立验证和验收。纯翻译、一般网页阅读、仅截图无功能验收、仅颜色间距对齐不触发。

interface.shortDescription: Independently accept delivered tests and user journeys
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $whitebox-verify for independent acceptance of delivered TestPack tests through real interactions, screenshots, and authoritative readback. Route test design, writing, generation, and repair to $test-authoring; report missing cases instead of authoring them.

skills.name: imagegen
skills.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

interface.shortDescription: Generate or edit images for websites, games, and more
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $imagegen to make or edit an image for this project.

skills.name: openai-docs
skills.description: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex.
skills.shortDescription: Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, and self-knowledge; OpenAI APIs and ChatGPT Work. 'You'/'this app' means Codex only.

interface.shortDescription: OpenAI and Codex docs for models, skills, tasks, and setup
interface.defaultPrompt: Use OpenAI Docs for official docs lookup, questions about Codex itself or Codex surfaces, model selection, model migration, and prompt-upgrade work.

skills.name: review-agent
skills.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.

interface.shortDescription: Find actionable bugs in code changes
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $review-agent to review the requested code changes and return actionable findings.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources.

interface.shortDescription: Create or update a skill

skills.name: skill-installer
skills.description: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos).
skills.shortDescription: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos

interface.shortDescription: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos
